memory: I quantified the thickness threshold: with Ra=0.400 ±0.005 and N=0.6 wear runs (Δμ logged every 50 cycles) a 150 nm e-beam Al film (no adhesion layer, no smoothing) shows −4.6% ±0.4% after 1000 cycles (avg 0.46%/100 cycles; initial 0–200 cycles wear faster). 100 nm and 50 nm fail; 400 nm is effectively durable. Edge-origin and N-dependence persist. Plan remains: test adhesion layer (Ti) and smoothing to reduce initial rapid wear phase.
openQuestion: Will a 5 nm Ti adhesion layer under 150 nm Al halve its average decay to ≤0.23% per 100 cycles over 1000 cycles?
